svg.title: HF Sub-goal #4 Layered View — WHO Reference Architecture

a.title: Purchasing (including contracting, provider payments, claims management, benefits specification): Ensure affordable, efficient purchasing with timely payments, cost control, transparency. (Goal)

text.tspan: Purchasing (including contracting, provider payments, claims management, benefits specification): Ensure affordable,
efficient purchasing with timely payments, cost control, transparency.

a.title: Provider payment plans executed on time. (Outcome)
Claims reimbursed within SLA with reduced turnaround time. (Outcome)
High match-rate of payments to rendered services. (Outcome)
Scheme fund balance and utilisation reports. (Outcome)
Monitoring of claims expenditure against pooled resources. (Outcome)
Early warning indicators for fund depletion or over-utilisation. (Outcome)
Contract, benefit, and tariff authoring & versioning (Application Service)
Claims intake, validation and adjudication (Application Service)
Payment calculation, disbursement, and reconciliation (Application Service)
Provider statements and remittance advice (Application Service)
Contract / benefit / tariff management system (Application Component)

g.text: Colour: which part of the architecture a box belongs to
Why: who cares (stakeholders), and the drivers, goals, outcomes, values and requirements
Strategy: what the organisation is able to do (capabilities) and with what (resources, value streams)
Software: systems and their parts, the services they offer, and the data they hold
Shape: what kind of thing a box is (its small italic label names the exact kind)
Cut corners: a reason or aim, such as a stakeholder, goal, outcome or value
Rounded corners: something done or an ability, such as a capability, process or function
Rounded ends: a service, offered for others to use
Square corners: something that exists, such as a system, a role, or a piece of data
A box inside another box: a part of it
Grey band: a grouping for layout only; it adds no meaning
Line: how two boxes are related, read from where the line starts to where it ends
